Human freedom consists in acting from the necessity of one's own nature, not in escaping causation.
Human bondage arises when passions and external causes overpower the power of reason.
Substance is that which exists in itself and is conceived through itself alone.
An attribute is what the intellect perceives of substance as constituting its essence.
God is a being absolutely infinite, a substance consisting of infinite attributes.
The human mind is part of the infinite intellect of God and reflects the body it animates.
The order and connection of ideas is the same as the order and connection of things.
An emotion is a confused idea by which the mind affirms a greater or lesser force of existing.
Joy is the passage of a man from a lesser to a greater perfection.
Sadness is the passage of a man from a greater to a lesser perfection.
Virtue is nothing but acting according to the laws of one's own nature.
The highest form of knowledge is the intuitive grasp of the essence of things.
The power of the mind is defined by adequate ideas alone, not by blind desire.
Nature has no fixed goal and all final causes are merely human fictions.
The mind is eternal insofar as it conceives things under a form of eternity.
Desire is the very essence of man in so far as it is conceived to be determined to action.
Reason demands nothing contrary to nature and so demands that each should love oneself.
The human body is composed of many individuals of different natures acting together.
A thing is called free which exists from the necessity of its own nature alone.
The final aim of ethics is to show how the mind may be led to blessedness through understanding.
